rule: A table without a static identity gives no name: a parameter, a reassigned local, a local bound to a call result or other expression, a computed index. A function stored into it, in either form, folds into the enclosing function, and calls on it stay `T.f`, low.
notes: Each `require` is an invocation of the loader: `_G#require`, medium, direct, on its line (Decisions 2026-11-10, CommonJS / Lua `require`). main.lua is not itself required; it sits at the require root (src/) that explains every require string in the case, so the name a require from that root gives it is `main` (Lua note: 'module = the name the scan's `require` strings give the file'). call_type convention (SPEC lists the types but gives no Lua mapping): a `:` call is method, a `.` or bare call is direct (the 2026-11-10 require ruling makes `_G#require` direct), a call through a value is callback. Four tables without static identity: parameter `obj` (`function obj.hook` and `obj.unhook = function`, both forms), local `T` reassigned on line 19, local `R` bound to a call result (setmetatable), and the computed index `handlers[name]`. Each stored function is not a node; the calls in its body (tostring, P.helper) fold into the enclosing named function. Calls on those tables stay `obj.hook`, `obj.unhook`, `T.go`, `R.run`, low. `local function make` is `plugin.make`.
